added_edges.relationship: Founded in 1952 through a coalition involving British Marxist historians to advance historical research for readers across periods, regions and specialisms.
added_edges.evidence_note: The link locates a journal-building initiative within Marxist social history while retaining its generalist purpose and participation beyond Marxism. It does not identify the journal as exclusively Marxist, date the birth of social history to 1952, or replace its separate narrative-debate edge.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1959 following the joint planning of SHOT and its journal, with a programme of bringing disciplines together in the history of technology.
added_edges.evidence_note: Participant recollections connect the 1958 institutional decision to the first-issue programme. The edge records institutional consolidation and interdisciplinary intent; older histories of technology are not erased and subsequent practice is not inferred from the manifesto.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1990 as the World History Association’s research journal to develop historical inquiry from a global perspective.
added_edges.evidence_note: The 1989 announcement directly states purpose and scheduled start; the accepted 1990 title record corroborates the launch. This is one institutional project within the atlas’s wider world/global/connected-history umbrella, not its unique origin or every later connected-history approach.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1975 with a programme connecting historical inquiry and social-scientific analysis through thematic issues, research reports and discussion.
added_edges.evidence_note: Uses the already reviewed four-author founding foreword. Historical social science is broader than Sonderweg; neither all later journal contents nor every contributor is assigned to a single doctrine. The announced editorial mechanisms are not an audit of implementation.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1916 under Carter G. Woodson and ASNLH to preserve, publish and expand knowledge of Black historical experience and contributions.
added_edges.evidence_note: Contemporary reception reproduced in volume 1 describes the recovery and documentation programme. This institutional milestone falls within the atlas’s earlier roots; Black historical thought predates the journal. The 1916 original title remains distinct from the 2002 Journal of African American History title.

findings.assessment: Dedicated account of professional/public practice and its methods; existing public-memory and oral-history approaches remain relevant.
Dedicated field trajectory connecting professional, social, patient and colonial histories; Roy Porter and African healing are already represented.
Dedicated account of urban historiography and its methodological disagreements; cities already occur in several substantive approaches.

limitations: Subject counts are checked candidate classifications, not worldwide totals or a ranking.
Examples are selected independently and need not carry the counted category.
A missing correspondence is a review lead, not proof of missing historical content.
Gap priorities are editorial assessments supported and qualified in the report.
